title: Greedy Covariate Selection for Conditional Optimal Transport Bounds in Gaussian Experiments
banked_reason: The exact Gaussian fixed-budget submodularity-ratio frontier is mathematically sound and subfield-worthy, but its 6.8 ceiling is below the 7.2 field floor; bounded positioning and related-work repairs cannot supply the stronger greedy-value, fixed-signal, integrated inference, or broader-class result needed to clear field.
gap_reasons: The exact fixed-budget frontier is the flagship theorem, but its node-level justification compares only with earlier internal inequalities; add a precise comparison to the closest published weak-submodularity/conditional-transport result class stating why none gives this two-arm Gaussian finite-budget equality frontier.

van der Vaart is cited as external substrate but has no relevance sentence in the related-work discussion; identify it there as the standard triangular-array CLT used only for the non-novel inference specialization.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the piecewise exact fixed-budget submodularity-ratio frontier, its induced greedy certificate, the matching unequal-scale Gaussian infimal construction, and both k=1 and R=1 elbows; the final math review passed after lawful attestation of van der Vaart's Lindeberg--Feller theorem. The field-tier claim collapsed because this is not a sharp worst-case greedy-value ratio: the witness has vanishing endpoint contrast, the empirical guarantee is conditional on an unquantified uniform-error event, and the inference results provide coverage without interval-length or whole-class informativeness guarantees. A future re-raise needs a genuinely stronger result such as a nonvanishing-signal greedy-value converse, justified broader-class transfer, or integrated informative finite-sample selection and inference, while preserving the two unrepaired positioning findings above.
tldr: For a randomized Gaussian experiment, the observed-law functional \(B(S)\) is the sharp conditional-optimal-transport lower endpoint for the causal estimand \(\tau_2\), not the estimand itself. Its increment is a squared chordal distance between upper-hemisphere lifts of residualized arm-score vectors. Writing \(K=M/m\) and \(R=V/s\), the exact fixed-budget submodularity-ratio frontier is \(\rho_k(K,R)=1\) when \(k=1\) or \(R=1\), and \(\rho_k(K,R)=k/\{1+(k-1)KR\}\) when \(k\ge2\) and \(R>1\). Hence population forward greedy attains the exact certified factor \(1-\{1-\rho_k(K,R)/k\}^k\), with the corresponding empirical additive-error guarantee. Unequal-scale Gaussian families attain the frontier in the limit, and the optimal dimension-free limit is \(1/(KR)\) for \(R>1\). Generic greedy analysis and sample-split post-selection inference are credited prior machinery; the new contribution is the sharp Gaussian budget frontier. Independent evaluation gives Wald inference on the separated parameter image and a conservative raw-moment projection interval over the whole compact image, including equality laws.
gap: Conditional optimal transport supplies sharp covariate-assisted causal bounds, but existing work treats the conditioning set as fixed. Generic weak-submodularity theory does not determine the approximation ratio of the unequal-scale two-arm Gaussian endpoint.
fill: The project derives that geometry, proves the optimal dimension-free margin certificate with a fully randomized unequal-scale lower family, transfers it to greedy selection, and formulates credited sample-split Wald inference on \(\Theta_+(\nu_*)\) together with projection inference on the full compact moment image \(\Theta\).
